Immigration Agent Shoots Dominican Man in New York
Society: Dominican Republic
Key Facts
—Who. Oscar Belgal, 28, a Dominican national, shot by a US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent. His 5-year-old child was in the back seat and was not physically hurt.
—What. An ICE officer fired seven rounds into his car during an immigration arrest operation, and he was hit in the neck. He is in stable condition.
—Where. Marble Hill, a neighbourhood on the northern tip of Manhattan that sits beside the Bronx, near West 225th Street. Protests followed outside NewYork-Presbyterian Allen Hospital.
—When. Around 4 p.m. on Thursday 8 October 2026. Further protests took place on Friday 9 October 2026.
—Status. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and New York officials give conflicting accounts. A federal judge has set a hearing on the man’s case.
—As of. 9 October 2026, 20:00 GMT.
An ICE agent shot and wounded a Dominican man in front of his 5-year-old child during an immigration arrest in New York City on Thursday 8 October 2026. Protests followed, and New York leaders demanded answers from Washington, which matters to US readers because the case tests federal immigration enforcement inside a city whose mayor opposes it.
What We Know
Commissioner Tisch said a plainclothes federal officer approached Belgal’s car with a weapon drawn as he pulled into a parking space. When the car moved forward, at least one officer fired seven rounds, according to NBC New York.
Belgal was struck in the neck, below the left ear, and taken to NewYork-Presbyterian Allen Hospital in Inwood. Tisch said he is in stable condition, and the child was not physically injured.
DHS said its officers were carrying out “a targeted enforcement operation” against a man from the Dominican Republic with a prior grand larceny conviction. It also cited earlier arrests, which we have not independently verified.
DHS says the man drove into officers’ vehicles and that they believed their lives were in danger, as reported by the Bronx Times. It also said officers “immediately rendered aid,” and NBC New York reports that DHS said it did not know a child was in the car.
The New York Police Department (NYPD) commissioner described the sequence of events at a news briefing. Civic leaders at the protest asked the agents involved to identify themselves.
How New York Leaders Responded
Mayor Zohran Mamdani said: “ICE shot a New Yorker while his five year old child was in the car.” He also said he spent two hours on the phone with President Donald Trump and DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin without winning the man’s release, according to ABC7 New York.
Governor Kathy Hochul said she spoke with both men and demanded “full transparency.” She asked for all body camera footage to be made public and urged federal authorities to halt ICE operations in New York.
Hundreds of people gathered outside the hospital on Thursday night, chanting “ICE out of NYC,” and police made arrests, according to ABC7 New York. Another protest was planned for Friday afternoon at Foley Square in Lower Manhattan.
Dominican media, including RNN in the Dominican Republic, reported the shooting as a case of a Dominican citizen wounded in New York. We did not find a statement from the Dominican foreign ministry or its New York consulate by the time of publication.
The Dispute Over What Happened
The accounts differ on a key point. Tisch described the car as moving forward, while DHS says the driver rammed its vehicles and endangered officers.
No video has been made public in the coverage we reviewed. Hochul’s call for body camera footage shows that the footage is likely to decide which account stands.
What Is Not Known
It is not known whether any agent will face an inquiry or discipline, or what the federal investigation will conclude. Belgal’s own account has not been published, and the DHS account of his record and of the shooting has not been tested in court.
NBC New York reports that he remains in ICE custody at an undisclosed location, and that his attorney has filed a federal petition. A judge set a hearing for Friday afternoon, but we found no Dominican government statement and no decision on his immigration case.
What It Means for Travelers and US Readers
Dominican New Yorkers form a large community, and many US readers have ties to it through family, work or travel. A confrontation of this kind can raise tension between city and federal authorities and affect how immigrant neighbourhoods deal with police.
Travelers with a Dominican or other immigration case should carry valid documents and follow official guidance from their own government. Protests in northern Manhattan and the Bronx have so far centred on the hospital and public squares, and local news and NYPD notices give the latest on street closures.

sources.news_title: Outrage erupts after ICE agent fires seven shots into car with 5-year-old inside
sources.text:
Outrage erupted in New York after a federal immigration officer fired seven shots at a car carrying a 5-year-old child, striking the driver in the neck during an attempted arrest that has prompted fierce criticism of Immigration and Customs Enforcement and renewed questions about the Trump administration’s enforcement tactics.
The shooting happened Thursday afternoon in Marble Hill, a Manhattan neighborhood, when plainclothes federal officers approached 28-year-old Oscar Belgal as he pulled into a parking space. According to New York City Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch, Belgal began moving the vehicle forward before at least one officer fired seven rounds. One bullet struck him below the left ear.
The child, who was in the back seat, was not injured.
Belgal survived and was taken to a hospital before federal authorities transferred him to a detention facility outside New York, according to reporting by the Associated Press and CBS New York.
The shooting triggered immediate protests and condemnation from city officials, who questioned why immigration officers were carrying out the operation in plain clothes and whether the use of deadly force was justified.
Mayor Zohran Mamdani called the shooting an outrage and demanded an end to federal immigration enforcement operations in the city. Gov. Kathy Hochul also criticized the incident and said she had raised her concerns with President Donald Trump and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin.
The administration, however, has forcefully defended the officers.
Federal officials say Belgal was the subject of a targeted enforcement operation and allege that he drove toward officers and rammed government vehicles, creating a danger to their safety. Mullin said Friday that the officers did not know a child was in the car.
The Department of Homeland Security also pointed to Belgal’s prior grand larceny conviction and pending drug-related case. Those allegations and his criminal history, however, do not by themselves resolve the central question surrounding the shooting: whether the officers’ use of force was justified under the circumstances.
The sequence of events remains a critical issue. City officials have said an NYPD security camera recorded some of the events leading up to the gunfire, although it did not capture the shooting itself. The NYPD later released body-camera footage showing officers arriving after the shots were fired and rushing Belgal to the hospital.
The federal officers involved were reportedly wearing plain clothes, masks and reflective construction-style vests, making it difficult for bystanders to identify them as law enforcement. That detail has added to concerns about how the operation unfolded in a public street with a young child in the vehicle.
The shooting also prompted demonstrations near the scene and at the hospital where Belgal was initially treated. Protesters condemned ICE’s tactics, while some clashes with police resulted in arrests.
The dispute has since widened into a confrontation between the Trump administration and New York officials over immigration enforcement. Federal authorities blamed so-called sanctuary policies for the incident, while city leaders argued that the operation raises serious questions about accountability and the use of force.
The incident comes amid a broader pattern of confrontations involving ICE officers and vehicles. The Associated Press has reported that ICE agents have fired their weapons during more than a dozen vehicle stops since last year, killing several people and wounding others.
The seven shots fired in Marble Hill are now at the center of a growing demand for answers. Officials and residents want a fuller account of what happened before the gunfire, what the officers knew, and what evidence supports the federal government’s justification.
With a child in the back seat and the driver shot in the neck, the stakes are unmistakable. The release of additional video and a transparent review of the shooting will be crucial to determining whether the use of force was warranted.

US immigration officials defend ICE agents who shot man in same car as child
- Published
US immigration officials have defended officers who shot and wounded a man in his car in New York on Thursday while his five-year-old son was in the back seat.
Department of Homeland Security (DHS) chief Markwayne Mullin said officers opened fire while trying to arrest a man with a criminal history.
"We weren't aware the child was in the car," Mullin said, arguing that it was the man, Oscar Belgal, who had put his child in danger. Belgal is being held at a detention facility. His lawyers appeared at a hearing on his behalf on Friday.
"The first thing he asked me, is whether his son is OK," his attorney Harold Solis said outside court.
A handful of friends and family members, including a cousin and an aunt, attended the hearing but did not speak to the press.
Another of his lawyers, Paige Austin, told the judge at the hearing that Belgal "still has a bullet in his body" and had been taken to the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn after being discharged from hospital.
Austin said he had only been able to make a brief phone call within the hour prior to the hearing.
The BBC has not been able to confirm his medical condition, but contacted DHS and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).
The shooting happened in the residential neighbourhood of Marble Hill.
Marcos Charles, a top ICE official, said the agency's officers used their vehicles to try and stop Belgal in his car but that he resisted orders to get out and instead accelerated, smashing into two ICE vehicles.
Charles said Belgal then "weaponised his vehicle and proceeded to accelerate going towards other officers", adding: "Our officers, using their training, and believing that their life and the life of their partners in the general public were in danger, used their training and fired weapons."
The number of officers who fired their weapons is being investigated.
Charles said Belgal "was struck by one of the bullets or fragments superficially in the neck".
New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who called what happened "unconscionable and incredibly serious", said ICE agents surrounded Belgal's car before opening fire.
"They wore construction vests and masks that concealed their faces. There is no reasonable way to identify them as ICE agents," Mamdani said. He confirmed the child was unharmed.
Mullin said the officers identified themselves and were wearing body-worn cameras that were turned on during the incident.
Video of the shooting, including body camera footage, has not been made public but unverified videos on social media appear to align with Mamdani's comments.
Body-worn camera footage released by the New York Police Department (NYPD) on Friday shows its officers arriving on scene and attempting to help Belgal after he has been shot. One ICE officer appears to be wearing a neon construction vest and carrying a large gun.
The NYPD officers then call for an ambulance and put him in a police car to take him to hospital. They are later seen pulling Belgal from the vehicle and carrying him into the hospital.
Mamdani said on Thursday that he had spoken to US President Donald Trump and Mullin for two hours but failed to negotiate Belgal's release.
Mamdani said he would ask Trump, who has not yet commented publicly on the shooting, to end ICE enforcement actions in New York. Mullin has said he will not pause enforcement.
The DHS said Belgal, 28, was from the Dominican Republic and had "a prior criminal conviction for grand larceny and multiple prior arrests for assault, robbery, possession of drugs and weapons possession".
Belgal was arrested by police officers in New York in December 2023 and released "a few days later", according to the DHS.
New York City Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said there was also still a pending case against Belgal for criminal sale of a controlled substance in 2025.
DHS has also alleged Belgal was associated with the Trinitarios, described by the US justice department as a transnational criminal group.
Mullin said the DHS believed Belgal "has either indirect or direct knowledge" of a US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) officer shooting, "and that's why he became a target".
Mamdani is not the only New York official to have criticised the incident. Governor Kathy Hochul said federal officials needed to provide answers quickly about what happened.
"New Yorkers have witnessed far too many acts of violence by a rogue federal agency and untrained agents that operate with impunity," Hochul said, adding that she had spoken to Mullin and Trump as well.
There have been several high-profile shootings involving ICE officers this year, including one that caused the death of Renee Good in Minneapolis in January.

sources.news_title: Protests Erupt in New York City After ICE Agent Shoots Man in the Bronx
sources.text:

A federal immigration officer shot a man Thursday afternoon in New York’s Marble Hill neighborhood, according to police, eyewitnesses and the Department of Homeland Security, in an incident that drew swift rebuke from elected officials and a crowd of spontaneous protesters late Thursday night.
The man was treated at a nearby hospital for a gunshot wound to the neck, officials said.
Eyewitnesses described a chaotic scene unfurling on a busy street in Marble Hill — a neighborhood that is legally in Manhattan but connected to The Bronx — around 4 p.m., as a slew of New Yorkers were getting home from work and school. As shots rang out, bystanders sheltered in neighboring businesses, the eyewitnesses said.
New York City officials said the ICE agents were in plainclothes wearing masks and construction vests at the time of the shooting, and video and photos of the moments after showed one agent brandishing an assault rifle, as passersby ducked for cover.
Crowds of protesters and elected officials arrived at the scene in the hours after the shooting and outside the nearby NewYork—Presbyterian Allen Hospital, where the wounded man was taken.
“What happened today was an outrage,” Mayor Zohran Mamdani said at a press conference at the scene late Thursday night. Mamdani confirmed the man’s 5-year-old son was in the car at the time of the shooting.
“When ICE agents opened fire, a 5-year-old child — a 5-year-old child — was in the back seat of that car,” he said. “Thank god that child is physically unharmed.”
The mayor said he spent two hours on the phone with President Donald Trump and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin in a failed attempt to get the shooting victim — identified as 28-year-old Oscar Belgal — released. Instead, Mamdani said, ICE agents “whisked him away” from the hospital in Upper Manhattan. 
“During the incident, an ICE officer discharged his weapon and the criminal illegal alien was injured,” the statement read. “ICE officers immediately rendered aid. The individual is alive and at a local hospital. The FBI and HSI are on the scene. The incident remains under investigation.”
Belgal was identified by Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch late Thursday. Court records showed he pleaded guilty in 2025 to grand larceny in the fourth degree and had an open charge for criminal possession of a controlled substance stemming from an arrest in 2025.
Eyewitnesses to the shooting spoke to The City Reporter and Documented in the hours after the shooting, recalling the commotion as gunfire erupted in the middle of a residential neighborhood. Iris Rosa, a school therapist, said after she emerged from a nearby shop, she saw a man bleeding on the ground in front of a car, while agents milled around, one holding a small child.
“He was all full of blood,” she said, while the child an agent held was quiet. “How could you do this? What is going on? And then I’m looking at the baby.”
Stephanie Ferrer, 30, who lives in Marble Hill, said she heard multiple shots and called 911. She watched the scene from one of her bedroom windows until agents carried the man away by his arms and legs.
“He was disoriented, I think because one of the guys that was holding him next to him was trying to keep him aware, trying to keep him awake by just doing some taps on the cheek,” she said. “You know, like, ‘hey buddy,’ like ‘stay awake, don’t fall asleep.’”
A video posted to social media appeared to show the chaotic aftermath, with a crowd gathered as NYPD officers rushed to a car and carried a man, seemingly unconscious, out of it and into the back of a law enforcement vehicle.
“Put pressure,” one officer is heard to say as they load the man into the back seat.
In a statement posted to X, the NYPD confirmed federal agents were behind the shooting and took the victim to the hospital. “The NYPD was not involved in the incident and was not on scene at the time of the shooting,” they said.
By Thursday evening a crowd of protesters had gathered at the scene, while NYPD officers and caution tape blocked off the street. The dented car Belgal was driving could still be seen blocking West 225th Street at Marble Hill Avenue. Two agents in plainclothes from the Department of Homeland Security were canvassing the area for video footage.
At an impromptu protest at the scene Thursday night elected officials and immigrant advocates gathered to denounce the shooting.
Rep. Adriano Espaillat told the crowd the child was safe with other family members and that he had tried to visit the wounded man in a nearby hospital and been barred from talking with him by ICE agents.
“The family is shaken…by this terrible horrible shooting,” he said.
Another crowd of protesters gathered outside the nearby NewYork-Presbyterian Allen Hospital where the man was said to have been taken, as police and officials from Mamdani’s office stood at the perimeter.
Protesters tried to block a car of federal agents leaving the hospital, and police officers pushed demonstrators aside to clear the way, making several arrests.
The shooting occurred not far from the rooftop parking deck of a Target store where, Bronx Borough President Vanessa Gibson said later that night, federal immigration agents sometimes muster, before heading into The Bronx to make arrests.
Jumaane Williams, the city’s public advocate, told Documented and The City Reporter that he spoke with the family of the shooting victim.
“Thankfully, the father is alert, from what I understand. Shot in the neck, but alive, which I’m thankful for, and his child is with the family,” said Williams. “But I don’t trust the investigation that the federal government is going to try to do.”
Mamdani called for ICE to be abolished and, referring to striking images of one of the agents standing at the shooting scene in a yellow construction vest and holding a rifle.
“Residents have no idea if these are law enforcement agents or if they are simply attacking someone on the street,” he said. “When it comes to ICE it begs the question, ‘What’s the difference?’”
Gov. Kathy Hochul said she had talked with President Donald Trump and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin about the shooting.
“I expressed outrage on behalf of New Yorkers and urged them to halt ICE enforcement operations in New York,” she said in a statement. “I also asked that any body camera footage of the shooting be released to the public so we can establish the facts and get to the truth.”

ICE Agent Shoots Person in Bronx With Child in the Car, Victim Is Hospitalized But Stable After Incident
Oct. 9 2026, Published 11:00 a.m. ET
An ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations agent shot and wounded a 28-year-old man during a targeted immigration enforcement operation in the Marble Hill neighborhood of the Bronx, New York City, on Thursday afternoon, October 8.
According to the Department of Homeland Security, ICE officers were attempting to box in the suspect's vehicle to make an arrest when the driver rammed the ICE vehicles. At least one federal agent opened fire, discharging multiple rounds into the car.
A 5-year-old child was sitting in the back seat of the vehicle during the gunfire. The child was physically uninjured and has since been reunited with relatives.
What Happened in the Bronx?
Law enforcement sources identified the man as Oscar Belgal, a citizen of the Dominican Republic. He suffered non-life-threatening injuries, including a graze wound to the neck, and is in stable condition at an area hospital.
DHS stated that Belgal has prior criminal convictions and arrests for robbery, drugs, and weapons, and has documented ties to the Trinitarios street gang.
This marks the first shooting involving ICE agents in New York City since President Donald Trump initiated his nationwide immigration enforcement crackdown. Nationally, federal immigration agents have shot at least 21 people since Trump took office, seven of them fatally, including mother Renee Good and nurse Alex Pretti.
Zohran Mamdani Condemns ICE
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani denounced the operation, calling the situation "unconscionable" due to the presence of the child and urging President Trump to halt localized ICE actions.

The Briefing:
- Oscar Belgal, 28, a Dominican national, was shot in the Marble Hill neighborhood shortly after 4 p.m. on Thursday, October 8, and transported to NewYork-Presbyterian Allen Hospital in stable condition.
- His 5-year-old son was seated in the back of the vehicle when the ICE agent opened fire; the child was physically unharmed and was placed in the care of a family member.
- Mayor Zohran Mamdani spent two hours calling both President Trump and DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin to seek Belgal's immediate release — those talks failed, and Belgal remained in ICE custody as of late Thursday night.
A federal immigration agent fired seven rounds into a vehicle parked on a Marble Hill residential street Thursday afternoon, striking a 28-year-old Dominican man in the neck while his young son sat inches away in the back seat — setting off a political firestorm that reached the White House by nightfall.
This is the first ICE-involved shooting in New York City since President Trump launched his second-term immigration enforcement surge, and it has immediately tested Mayor Zohran Mamdani's ability to shield immigrant communities in a city caught between federal authority and local outrage.
Seven Shots, One Block, One Child
NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch confirmed at a late-night press conference that the ICE agent discharged seven rounds. Belgal was struck below his left ear — a graze wound to the neck — and arrived at the hospital conscious and in stable condition. The NYPD was not involved in the operation and was not on scene when shots were fired, Tisch said. Officers arrived afterward to find Belgal handcuffed and seated on the ground; they rendered aid and transported him.
Tisch also said that an NYPD security camera recorded events leading up to the gunfire but did not capture the shooting itself — a gap in the record that lawyers and civil rights advocates are already contesting. The bullet left an entry point on the vehicle's front windshield and an exit point in one of the rear windows.
Tisch said Belgal had been pulling into a parking space on Marble Hill Avenue near West 225th Street when a plainclothes federal officer approached with a gun drawn, followed by a second agent also out of uniform. Belgal then pulled the car forward, and at least one officer fired. That account, however, is contested: two law enforcement sources told NBC News that Belgal had attempted to ram his vehicle into the ICE officers before the shots were fired.
The 5-year-old — believed to be Belgal's son — was located safe and placed with a family member, according to a law enforcement source. "Thank God that child is physically unharmed," Mayor Mamdani told reporters, his voice carrying the weight of a neighborhood still absorbing what it had witnessed.
DHS Defends the Operation — Then Quietly Rewrites Its Statement
The Department of Homeland Security defended the enforcement action by pointing to Belgal's criminal record: a prior conviction for grand larceny and multiple prior arrests on charges including assault, robbery, drug possession, and weapons possession. In its original Thursday evening statement, DHS also stated that Belgal had ties to the Trinitarios, a Dominican street gang the Trump administration has used as the central justification for its Operation Salvo enforcement surge across New York City.
But by early Friday, that Trinitarios reference had been quietly removed from DHS's official statement, according to AFP — without explanation. The agency has not publicly clarified what prompted the deletion, nor has it explained why seven shots were necessary during a daytime operation in a residential neighborhood with a child inside the vehicle.
Federal officials said ICE agents rendered aid to Belgal immediately after the shooting. Electronic court records show that Belgal had pleaded not guilty in a pending drug case.
Mamdani Goes to Marble Hill — and Calls Trump
Mayor Mamdani did not wait until morning. He traveled to Marble Hill Thursday night, flanked by elected officials, and delivered a statement drawing a hard line. "We want ICE out of our city, ICE out of our schools, ICE out of our hospitals, ICE out of our streets, ICE away from our kids," he said.
He confirmed spending two hours on the phone with President Trump and DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin seeking Belgal's immediate release from federal custody. The White House did not yield. Mamdani called the shooting a reflection of what ICE does in communities across the country on a daily basis and demanded Trump halt all immigration enforcement operations in New York City.
Time magazine noted the incident places direct pressure on Mamdani's relationship with the Trump administration — a dynamic the Democratic mayor had carefully managed since taking office in January. Congressman Adriano Espaillat also reported being denied access, along with Belgal's family members, to visit the wounded man at the hospital.
Elected Officials and Community React
City Council Member Carmen De La Rosa, whose District 10 includes Marble Hill, Washington Heights, and Inwood, called the shooting devastating. "We are heartbroken and enraged," said De La Rosa, a Democrat who herself emigrated from the Dominican Republic. Congressman Ritchie Torres, who represents the Bronx, posted that discharging multiple rounds into a vehicle with a child inside, on a busy residential street, is "abhorrent and indefensible."
Residents who gathered near the silver SUV on Marble Hill Avenue Thursday evening confronted federal agents directly; more than 300 protesters later marched to NewYork-Presbyterian Allen Hospital where Belgal was being treated. In Washington Heights and the Bronx — home to one of the largest Dominican communities in the United States — the shooting registered not just as news, but as a warning.
A Nationwide Pattern That Is Not Slowing Down
The Marble Hill shooting did not happen in a vacuum. City & State New York reported that at least two dozen people have been shot by ICE agents nationwide as part of Trump's deportation campaign since January 2025, citing The New York Times. An ABC News tally of shootings by federal immigration agents during Trump's second term reached at least 21 before Thursday's Bronx incident, with eight of those proving fatal — including three U.S. citizens.
This is also at least the second documented case in which a minor was present during an ICE shooting under the current enforcement surge — a pattern that immigration advocates say is now defining the administration's reach into everyday family life.
With the national conversation about ICE use-of-force intensifying by the week, Marble Hill Avenue — a stretch of sidewalk 26 days before the 2026 midterm elections — has become the most politically charged block in New York City.

Guests
- Darializa Avila ChevalierDemocratic nominee for New York’s 13th Congressional District.
- Carmen De La RosaNew York city councilmember representing the neighborhoods of Marble Hill, Inwood and Washington Heights.
Protests have erupted in New York City after a federal immigration agent shot and wounded a man in the Bronx on Thursday afternoon. As masked agents reportedly posing as construction workers attempted to arrest 28-year-old Oscar Belgal, they opened fire on his car. Belgal was shot in the neck. His 5-year-old child, who was in the back seat, was physically unharmed. Belgal was taken to a local hospital, where hundreds, including our guests, Democratic congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier and New York City Councilmember Carmen De La Rosa, gathered to demand his release.
“What we saw yesterday was a prime example of why [ICE] is a terror to our communities, why it should not exist,” says Avila Chevalier. She was among multiple people assaulted by officers with the NYPD unit that specializes in protest policing, known as the Strategic Response Group (SRG). Four others were arrested at Thursday evening’s protest. Avila Chevalier, who was knocked down to the ground by officers, says, “This is why we also must demand that we get rid of and disband the SRG, because this type of response should have never happened for folks who were just simply trying to protect their neighbor.”
“I personally witnessed the NYPD escalating aggressively towards our community, barricading the community in … I also witnessed NYPD helping the ICE vehicles whisk away our neighbors and come in and out of the hospital,” adds De La Rosa.
“We have become less safe with the presence of ICE, and we need to make sure that we are actually upholding the sanctuary policies of the city. There is no reason why NYPD should be collaborating this way,” says Avila Chevalier.
Transcript
AMY GOODMAN: Well, today, Juan, we’re going to be talking about your old neighborhood uptown in Manhattan. Protests erupted in New York City on Thursday after a federal immigration agent shot and wounded a man in his vehicle in the Marble Hill neighborhood of northern Manhattan. Seven shots rang out in quick succession just after 4 p.m. on a crowded street as people walked home from work or accompanied their children home from school. Twenty-eight-year-old Oscar Belgal was struck in the neck. His 5-year-old child was in the back seat of the car.
Belgal was taken to the nearby Columbia Presbyterian Allen Hospital, where hundreds of protesters gathered to demand his release, chanting ”ICE off our streets now!” and “We want justice!” New York police arrested four people, assaulted others, including congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier, who was knocked to the ground. She’ll join us in a minute.
In a late-night news conference, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said he called President Trump and spoke to him for two hours, and also talked to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, to negotiate Belgal’s release, but was unsuccessful.
MAYOR ZOHRAN MAMDANI: Around 4 p.m. this afternoon, a New Yorker was shot by ICE agents in Marble Hill. Many of the facts surrounding this shooting are still unclear. ICE agents surrounded the man’s vehicle before opening fire. They wore construction vests and masks that concealed their faces. There was no reasonable way to identify them as ICE agents.
School had just gotten out. The street was crowded with families and children. When ICE agents opened fire, a 5-year-old child — a 5-year-old child — was in the back seat of the car. Thank God, that child is physically unharmed.
For the past two hours, I have been on the phone with President Trump and Secretary Mullin negotiating the release of the man ICE agents shot. Those negotiations were unsuccessful. Just moments ago, ICE put the man in an unmarked vehicle and whisked him away.
Let me say this plainly: What happened today was an outrage. I stand here not just as the mayor of our city, but as someone who is proud to be an immigrant in our city. And I know that these kinds of raids, this kind of terrorizing of this city, leaves the 3 million immigrants of this city asking if they are safe here, if they belong here, if this, too, can be their home here.
We will not normalize ICE’s viciousness. We will not accept its cruelty. We know, and I have said this directly, whether to the president or to the public, ICE undermines public safety. It makes us less safe. New York City will not stand by while ICE agents shoot New Yorkers, and we will not back down from the demand that so many, including myself, have put forward time and again. This is an agency that must be abolished.
AMY GOODMAN: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani late last night at a news conference.
We’re joined now by two guests who were also on the scene last night. New York City Councilmember Carmen De La Rosa represents Marble Hill, Inwood and Washington Heights. And we’re joined by Darializa Avila Chevalier. She’s the Democratic candidate for Congress representing Upper Manhattan and parts of the Bronx.
I mean, to say the least, it was heated last night. I was there with Democracy Now!'s Nicole Salazar. Let me turn to Darializa Avila Chevalier. Can you talk about what you're demanding right now? As you participated in the news conference, then you marched to the hospital, hundreds were there. And then, what happened to you?
DARIALIZA AVILA CHEVALIER: Yeah, well, first of all, thank you, Amy, so much for having me. I had hoped that the next time we would get to speak would be under happier circumstances. But frankly, I’ve just been feeling enraged since yesterday, and it has been hard to process all that has happened and transpired.
You know, when we were at the press conference, we were calling very clearly, all of the elected officials, for the abolishment of ICE. This is an agency that should have never existed to begin with. And what we saw yesterday was a prime example of why it is a terror to our communities, why it should not exist. It undermines public safety. It makes our communities feel terrorized by their own government. And we need to make sure that such an agency never comes to pass and never exists again.
The fact that there were so many agents, ICE agents, HSI agents, federal agents, on the scene — the NYPD was not giving elected officials much information once we were on the scene to try to understand what had happened, whether or not the child was safe, the fact that it took so long for us to to get confirmation of those details, you know, all of that undermines public safety. Folks were scared, and rightfully so.
You know, it was — Senator Gustavo Rivera and I had to go behind HSI agents, Homeland Security Investigation agents, because they were going door to door asking neighbors for, quote-unquote, “evidence,” asking them about their video cameras, asking them for more information. And we had to go behind the HSI agents to let folks know that they were under no obligation to open the door, that they were under no obligation to speak to any of these agents without a warrant. And so, I want New Yorkers to know, if you see someone, even though it says “police,” if it’s not a warrant, if they do not have a warrant, they do not have to open the door or speak to any of these agents. They will pretend to be NYPD police. They are not. You do not have to open the door to them.
We, you know, went over to the press conference after that, called for abolishing ICE, called for the release of the person who had been shot, and for answers and accountability, and meaningful accountability. Unfortunately, what I saw was NYPD escalating the situation where protesters were outside of the hospital trying to make sure that ICE wasn’t leaving with our neighbor. And, you know, they continued to escalate the situation. As I was trying to deescalate and telling them that the barricades were not necessary, that folks were calm, you know, the tensions continued to rise, and police became more aggressive and, at one point, shoved me and others to the ground.
You know, there were four arrests that happened yesterday. Those were completely unnecessary. The escalation, you know, was completely unnecessary. And this is why we also must demand that we get rid of and disband the SRG, because this type of response should have never happened for folks who were just simply trying to protect their neighbor.
JUAN GONZÁLEZ: Yeah, I’d like to ask Councilwoman Carmen De La Rosa — I know this neighborhood well. I lived in Inwood, a few blocks away from there, for nearly 20 years. Especially around where this happened, this is a highly congested area, especially in the afternoon, at 4:00 in the afternoon, people coming out of the train station, a big mall right next door to there. Haven’t you and other public officials complained about — previously about ICE using a Target right there in that mall to gather their forces and to go out on sweeps?
CARMEN DE LA ROSA: Yes, there’s been an escalating sightings of ICE at the Target parking lot, which is private property. Myself and the surrounding elected officials have come together to demand that the owner of the property stop allowing ICE onto his property. We’ve been told that they would discontinue any presence of ICE at the parking lot. Unfortunately, we continue to see ICE there. And it has also been the scene of neighbors protesting that presence of ICE. But we’ve also seen ICE in our local parks. We’ve seen ICE sightings and congregating at Van Cortlandt Park and Inwood Hill Park. And this is the result of that escalating presence and unnecessary presence of ICE in our communities.
JUAN GONZÁLEZ: And how did the New York City Police Department deal with you as compared to the ICE agents and the federal authorities?
CARMEN DE LA ROSA: As Darializa just said, the information coming from the NYPD was vague at best. I personally witnessed the NYPD escalating aggressively towards our community, barricading the community in, pressing barricades against our neighbors as they tried to make sure that their rights, their civil rights to protest, to show up, to speak up, were were being violated. And unfortunately, I also witnessed NYPD helping the ICE vehicles whisk away our neighbors and come in and out of the hospital. So, in my opinion, although we have been told that NYPD does not collaborate, there is a perception of, at the very least, coordinating efforts for ICE’s entrance and exits into our hospital.
AMY GOODMAN: Darializa Avila Chevalier, witnesses have said that the ICE agent used what appeared to be a long gun, a large semi-automatic assault rifle. Can you talk about using a high-powered weapon as children are leaving school? And what does it mean for the city and also the state of New York to be a sanctuary city and state?
DARIALIZA AVILA CHEVALIER: You know, Amy, I cannot think of any good reason why such a weapon would be in our city at all, held by anybody, and the fact that these — these cowboys, who think they can just be above the law, are shooting into our streets, not asking who is around, shooting into a car that had a 5-year-old child in it. That child is so traumatized now because they just witnessed their — his father be shot by these agents.
You know, when we arrived at the scene, I asked the officers whether it was a crime scene because of the crash or a crime scene because of the shooting. And they told — the NYPD told me that it was a crime scene because of the shooting, and yet they could not tell us whether the shooter had been apprehended, who the shooter was. No information was given to us.
And so, to Carmen’s point, the vagueness of this really forces us to ask whether the silence here is not also complicity in ICE’s actions. The fact that, you know, we saw agents change clothes, we were trying to figure out, identify which agency they were with, and no information was being given to elected officials at all levels of government. It was truly astonishing, as I was making my way over to the hospital, to see, you know, an unmarked car, which had police lights, heading south, and police, NYPD police, pushing protesters, physically pushing protesters, out of the street as the car was ramming into people before speeding away. It is truly shocking. And, you know, the levels of violence, not just from the fact that the ICE agent had a weapon of that magnitude, but the use of the vehicles that were running into our neighbors, all of that, all of that, is an affront to the notion that this has anything to do with public safety. We have become less safe with the presence of ICE, and we need to make sure that we are actually upholding the sanctuary policies of the city. There is no reason why NYPD should be collaborating this way, even just by standing around. That, in itself, is complicity in this.
And, you know, I was actually very disgusted to hear Commissioner Tisch’s remarks yesterday, because just a few hours prior, Public Advocate Jumaane Williams reminded us that the way that the victim would be spoken about would be in a demonizing way, and just a few hours later, that is what Police Commissioner Tisch did. There was no reason for her to read out, you know, this person’s past contact with police. There was no justification for anything that transpired that afternoon. And for her to do that was symboling that there are some occasions under which that is OK. There is no occasion under which this is OK. There is no excuse for allowing ICE to come into our city to shoot seven bullets into cars where there are children. It is just an outrage, and I truly have no words for just how enraging everything that transpired last night was.
AMY GOODMAN: I want to thank you both for being with us, Darializa Avila Chevalier, Democratic candidate in New York’s 13th Congressional District, and I want to thank New York City Councilmember Carmen De La Rosa.
Coming up, the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize has been awarded to Navi Pillay, the South African-born jurist and human rights activist. Stay with us.

ICE officer shoots Dominican man during New York arrest, sparking protests
A federal immigration officer shot and wounded a Dominican man during an arrest in New York City. The incident set off protests, political backlash and renewed scrutiny of ICE tactics.
A federal immigration officer shot and wounded a Dominican man during an arrest in New York City on Thursday, in what the Department of Homeland Security described as a "targeted enforcement operation". The man survived and is being treated in hospital, while the agency said only that "during the incident, an ICE officer discharged his weapon" and that the man was injured.
The shooting drew sharp political reaction and protests, with critics calling it an example of the dangers of the Trump administration's immigration crackdown. Mayor Zohran Mamdani called it "unconscionable and incredibly serious", while New York Governor Kathy Hochul said the state wanted answers.
According to Mamdani and Hochul, they received reports that agents fired at the man while he was inside a vehicle with a five-year-old child, who was apparently not hurt. Mamdani said he intended to tell President Donald Trump to end all federal immigration enforcement actions in the city.
The gunfire broke out at about 4 pm in Marble Hill. Pedro Almaraz, who works at a nearby restaurant, said he heard three or four gunshots and then saw a man on the ground surrounded by several officers wearing face masks and vests bearing Department of Homeland Security branding. He said witnesses were screaming. Videos and photographs posted on social media showed a man sitting on the ground with his hands behind his back shortly after the shooting. Another video showed New York City police officers carrying an apparently injured man into a police vehicle. A damaged car with small holes in two windows was seen blocking the road nearby. The videos also showed agents at the scene wearing ICE badges, including one carrying a rifle.
At a tense press conference at the scene on Thursday night, several local politicians condemned the shooting. City Council member Carmen De La Rosa said, "We are heartbroken and enraged." Demonstrators chanted, "ICE off our streets now!" before marching to the hospital where the injured man was being treated. A large crowd blocked an intersection outside the hospital, and when police began putting up barricades to allow ambulances and other vehicles through, some protesters pushed the barriers and threw water bottles at officers. Police made some arrests.
DHS said its officers are "forced to make arrests at large in the community in unpredictable and dangerous environments" when "dangerous illegal aliens" are released, and blamed "reckless sanctuary policies" in Democratic-led areas. The agency described the man as a "criminal illegal alien" with a previous grand larceny conviction and a history of other arrests, and said New York police had arrested him in December 2023 before releasing him.
The shooting also renewed scrutiny of ICE tactics. ICE agents have fired their weapons during more than a dozen vehicle stops since last year, killing at least four people and wounding others. In late September, ICE told its officers not to engage in high-speed car chases and to carry out vehicle stops only if they had completed specific training.
Marble Hill resident Alfred Silva, 38, said federal officers should identify themselves more clearly, adding that one officer was wearing a construction safety vest and carrying a rifle. "We need to have better transparency to understand who we're dealing with, because anybody in the street can just put on a vest and pull out a gun and claim to be ICE," he said. "I feel like regardless if you're left or right, we should understand that this shouldn't be happening." In a statement, Hochul said New Yorkers were outraged, immigrant communities were terrified and the state wanted answers. She said, "New Yorkers have witnessed far too many acts of violence by a rogue federal agency and untrained agents that operate with impunity." The shooting left a man in hospital, triggered protests and political condemnation, and raised fresh questions over federal immigration enforcement in the city.

An Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent on the scene of a shooting in upper Manhattan on Thursday has repeatedly been accused in federal court of unlawful arrests and using force during arrests in New York and Minneapolis, a WIRED investigation finds.
On Thursday afternoon, ICE agents shot a man, identified by city authorities as Oscar Belgal, in Manhattan’s Marble Hill neighborhood, near the Bronx. Mayor Zohran Mamdani said agents surrounded the man’s car, in which a 5-year-old child was sitting, before firing multiple rounds—as many as seven, witnesses told local media. Belgal, the New York Police Department said, was hospitalized after reportedly being shot in the neck. The child appeared unharmed.
Footage from the scene shows a man in a high-visibility yellow construction vest brandishing a modified AR-15-style rifle with a pistol grip, sling, and holographic sights. That man, according to court documents, social media posts, and publicly available personal information reviewed by WIRED, is Brenden Cuni—an ICE supervisor with the agency’s National Fugitive Operations team who has been involved in several arrests in the New York City region and Minneapolis during Operation Metro Surge last winter.
Cuni identified himself as an ICE agent to NYPD officers, a law enforcement source tells WIRED, and was the only federal agent captured on video brandishing a weapon on scene. In a statement, the Department of Homeland Security claims that ICE agents were attempting to apprehend an undocumented immigrant from the Dominican Republic with a prior conviction for grand larceny.
A WIRED review of federal court cases, social media, and other public records suggests that Cuni has repeatedly been at the center of illegal ICE street arrests in New York and beyond. Court filings accuse him of using a Taser on a handcuffed man, while activists have alleged he is one of the agents seen forcing a pregnant woman to the ground during a Minneapolis operation. In recent months, federal judges have repeatedly found arrests involving Cuni unlawful. One judge called an arrest warrant he signed “fraudulent,” while another said that video evidence contradicts his sworn account of an arrest; in a third case, the government withdrew his sworn statements as inaccurate.
Cuni has been a DHS agent for nearly a decade. According to court declarations he signed, Cuni began his federal law enforcement career with Customs and Border Protection as a Border Patrol agent in San Diego in 2018 before becoming a deportation officer in 2020. In December 2024, he was promoted to a supervisory detention and deportation officer, and in May 2025, he joined the National Fugitive Operations team.
Cuni’s work history before his time with DHS remains unclear. Felician University, a private Catholic university in New Jersey, listed him as a member of its 2018 baseball roster. On that site, Cuni lists his hometown as New Rochelle—a suburb just north of the Bronx.
Cuni has been named in multiple lawsuits alleging violent arrests, both first reported last spring by The City and Documented as part of an investigation into hundreds of ICE street arrests in the New York area. Lawyers for a 21-year-old Bronx man claim that during his arrest in October last year, Cuni tripped him hard enough to break a tooth, then shocked him with a Taser about six times while he was handcuffed on the ground, and later called him a “maldito Mexicano”—damned Mexican. A medical record, obtained by THE CITY and Documented, noted injuries “from taser by ICE agents.”
The following month, another man alleged that ICE agents tackled and shocked him with a Taser three times during an arrest in Queens. According to the man’s petition, ICE’s arrest report lists Cuni among the arresting officers and acknowledges agents used a Taser. The filings do not say who fired it.
Court records also place Cuni in Minneapolis last December, leading a three-person ICE team at a scene where 60 to 70 people had gathered. Agents were trying to arrest a woman who had spray-painted an ICE vehicle; she escaped. Federal prosecutors charged a protester at the scene with assaulting Cuni, alleging that the man had helped tackle him after Cuni pepper-sprayed him. A judge later dismissed that charge with prejudice, writing that the evidence was “weak” and that none of the federal officers who reviewed videos of the encounter “saw a ‘tackle’ or other kind of assault.” Activists later alleged that Cuni was one of the agents seen in video of the encounter forcing to the ground a woman they say was pregnant. WIRED could not independently confirm that identification.
In at least three federal cases this year, judges or the government have found problems with Cuni’s statements or arrest paperwork. In one case, Judge Gary Brown of the Eastern District of New York found that Cuni searched five databases for a Bronx man and found nothing, then signed a warrant saying the searches had confirmed he was undocumented. ICE later added the man to those databases and searched again, creating the record Cuni had said already existed. Brown ruled the arrest and detention illegal, saying that Cuni had tried to “reconcile these falsehoods” after the fact.
In August, US District Judge Brian Cogan, also of New York’s Eastern District, said doorbell footage “largely contradicts” Cuni’s account of Fernando Fabian Chaglla’s arrest. Video reviewed by WIRED shows Chaglla being handcuffed less than three minutes into the encounter. Cuni later said he had typed Chaglla’s name and birth date into Mobile Fortify, an ICE face-recognition app; the search showed no record of lawful entry, but it did show a federal work permit. Cuni said he took the lack of records documenting his entry into the US as evidence that Chaglla was undocumented and acknowledged that he handcuffed him before filling out the warrant by hand. Cogan ruled that the arrest was unlawful.
A little over a week later, Cuni testified that he didn’t recall himself or the agents under his command ever making a warrantless arrest. “In all of the cases that I am aware of, I issued an I-200 prior to the arrest,” he assured the attorneys deposing him. “Now, if you’re questioning my credibility, I don’t know, but again, I’m—can only tell you what I’m aware of.”
In a third case, in June, government lawyers withdrew what a federal judge described as “inaccurate, sworn representations” by Cuni and other officials, including a claim that a detained man had skipped his ICE check-ins.
Cuni did not immediately respond to WIRED’s multiple requests for comment.
An Instagram account apparently associated with Cuni, previously using the handle “shooter.cuni”—now “shooter.914,” seemingly reflecting the Westchester County, New York, area code—contains scores of photographs and videos of Cuni with firearms at shooting ranges across the Northeast. Among the items depicted on the account are a mug that appears to be from ICE’s New York City Fugitive Operations team, a silver and black Rolex watch that closely matches one Cuni appears to be wearing in videos from the Marble Hill shooting, and an AR-15–style rifle with a pistol grip, short barrel, holoscopic sights, and olive-colored sling that appears to match the one he wielded at the shooting scene.
Another photo on the Cuni-linked Instagram account, posted on September 4, depicts a GA Precision Templar VII bolt-action rifle with a telescopic sight mounted on a bipod stand at a gun range. “Cuni” is emblazoned on a suede cushion on the rifle’s stock, and a blue “shooter Cuni” lanyard is visible on a separate cloth ammunition sling. The post’s caption reads, “the finest form of relaxation.”

sources.news_title: New York man shot in car by ICE agents with child present, Mamdani says
sources.text:
U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents shot and wounded a man on Thursday in his car with a child present in the vehicle in the Bronx borough of New York City, according to the mayor, city police and eyewitness accounts.
“Early reports indicate agents surrounded (the man) and a five-year-old-child in his car before firing multiple rounds,” New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said in a statement.
The mayor said the child was believed to have been physically unharmed. He referred to the man shot as a “New Yorker.”
“This is an unconscionable and incredibly serious situation,” Mamdani said, adding he had called U.S. President Donald Trump to talk about the incident. “When we speak I will demand that he ends all ICE enforcement actions in our city. I will not stand by while ICE agents terrorize our communities.”
ICE did not immediately respond to a request from Reuters for comment on the incident.
The incident was first reported on X by the New York Police Department, which gave few details other than to say: “there was a shooting involving federal law enforcement agents,” and that the person shot was “currently conscious and receiving medical attention.”
The shooting occurred at around 4 p.m. ET in the Marble Hill neighbourhood of the Bronx, the NYPD said.
An NYPD spokesperson said the agents involved in the shooting were part of DHS, the parent agency for Immigration and Customs Enforcement, the Customs and Border Protection and Border Patrol agencies, among others, and that federal authorities were investigating.
Pedro Almarez, owner of a nearby eatery, said he was working at the restaurant when he heard shots fired and went outside to see several officers wearing ICE attire at the scene.
“There were a lot of ICE officers, three or four cars,” Almarez told Reuters by phone, adding the man who was shot appeared to be between 20 and 30 years of age. He said NYPD officers arrived about 10 minutes later.
The city police department said its officers were not involved in the shooting.
At the shooting scene, where police strung yellow crime-scene tape to cordon off a city block, a woman standing on a balcony overlooking the area was heckling officers below about “taking our children.”

sources.news_title: New Yorkers get into heated confrontation with ICE agents who nearly hit 5-year-old boy in shooting
sources.text:
Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents shot a man in an SUV on a bustling New York City street Thursday afternoon as a 5-year-old boy sat in the vehicle’s backseat, sparking a heated confrontation between the feds and outraged citizens, officials said.
One ICE agent fired seven rounds into the silver Honda Civic at about 4 p.m. on Marble Hill Ave. near West 225th Street in the Bronx, hitting the victim in the neck, NYPD Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said at a late-night press conference at the scene.
The Department of Homeland Security said on X that the wounded man was “a criminal illegal alien from the Dominican Republic” that ICE had been searching for.
Mayor Mamdani said the boy was in the backseat of the SUV when ICE agents, who were wearing “construction vests and masks that concealed their faces,” started firing.
“There was no reasonable way to identify them as ICE agents,” Mamdani said. “Thank God, that child is physically unharmed. For the past two hours, I have been on the phone with President Trump and (U.S. Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne) Mullin, negotiating the release of the man ICE agents shot. Those negotiations were unsuccessful.”
After the man was treated at New York Presbyterian Allen Hospital, ICE agents “put the man in an unmarked vehicle and whisked him away,” Mamdani said.
Video posted online shows protesters being shoved out of the way of an unmarked black sedan as it was leaving the hosptial.
“What happened today was an outrage,” the mayor said. “We know that ICE is rotten to its core. Today’s shooting is only further devastating confirmation of what we have long known.”
Tisch said that the NYPD recovered surveillance camera footage that shows two ICE agents approaching their suspect as he backed into an empty parking space by a fire hydrant.
“One plainclothes federal law enforcement officer approaches the driver’s side window with his gun drawn,” Tisch said, describing the footage. “Another plainclothes officer also approaches the vehicle by the driver’s side headlight. The vehicle then starts to move forward and goes out of camera view.”
The shooting was not caught on camera, Tisch said. The man ICE shot has been arrested twice in New York City: one for robbery in 2023, in which he pleaded guilty to fourth-degree grand larceny and was sentenced to five years’ probation, and one for a drug sale in 2025. That case is still pending, Tisch said.
“Any trained law enforcement officer knows how easily that could have ended in tragedy,” Gov. Hochul said about the shooting on X. “By the grace of God, that child appears to have escaped without physical injury.
“No child should ever have to experience the terror of gunfire, let alone wonder if they’ll make it home alive,” she wrote. “As a mother and grandmother, I cannot imagine how frightening those moments must have been.”
More than 300 outraged New Yorkers held a protest at the scene, then marched to New York Presbyterian Allen Hospital, trapping ICE agents inside the building.
Protesters grabbed metal barriers blocking off the street and charged a row of cops before the officers were able to pull the barriers away from them. At least three people were taken into custody at the hospital, the NYPD said. Charges were pending.
Bronx Fruit vendor Cesar Gomez was down the block from the shooting Thursday afternoon when he heard a “zoom and the car crashed.”
“It was too many shots. Boom! Boom! Boom!” Gomez, 67, recalled. “(The victim) was bleeding from the back by his neck. They didn’t wait; they put him in their own unmarked car and took him to the hospital.”
Gomez said that masked ICE agents were armed with assault weapons.
“It wasn’t a pistol,” he said. “It was a long gun like an AK-47. They were masked. Everything was covered. It was really crazy.”
Witness Iris Rosa was coming home from work when she heard the shots and took cover.
“We were hiding and, when I came out, I saw the man sitting on the floor. He was in handcuffs,” Rosa, 76, said. “There was a child in the car, a boy. They pulled him out of the car. The baby was in shock. Didn’t cry, nothing.”
An ICE agent “with a huge gun” stood over the man on the ground, “then he started walking up and down like he owned the street,” Rosa said.
Rosa managed to speak with the wounded man, she said.
“They shot me! They tried to kill me!” he told Rosa.
“I’m disgusted. I never thought I’d live through this,” Rosa said. “I never thought this was happening in the U.S.”
DHS confirmed the wounded man has a prior criminal conviction for grand larceny, and “multiple prior arrests for assault, robbery, possession of drugs, and weapons possession.”
Their target also had “associations to the Trinitarios gang,” DHS said, although they didn’t identify him by name.
“During the incident, an ICE officer discharged his weapon and the criminal illegal alien was injured,” DHS said, adding that their suspect “was arrested by the NYPD on December 7, 2023, but was released into the community a few days later by reckless Democrat sanctuary policies that put American lives at risk.”
“ICE officers immediately rendered aid,” DHS said. “The individual is alive and at a local hospital. The incident remains under investigation.”
A video reviewed by the Daily News shows NYPD officers, who showed up after receiving multiple 911 calls about the incident, carrying the wounded man from the silver SUV and putting him into the back of a black car, which sped off.
A man with a federal badge around his neck sporting an assault rifle was in the middle of the street, asking witnesses taking video of the scene to back away, the video showed.
The NYPD “was not involved in the incident,” Tisch said.
The child was given to an aunt who lived on the block. He was not harmed, but his mother took him to a hospital to get evaluated, the aunt said.
After the shooting, throngs of outraged Bronx residents flocked to the corner shortly after the shooting, chanting “Murderers!” “F— ICE!” and “ICE out of the Bronx!”
During one heated exchange, more than a dozen people grabbed and pinned a masked ICE agent against a wall when he got too close to the police tape lining the scene.
NYPD officers swooped in and rescued the agent, pulling him back behind the tape as federal agents created a blockade line.
Assemblyman Manny De Los Santos (D-Manhattan), who showed up at the scene, was told that ICE agents weren’t cooperating with the NYPD.
“The ICE agents are over there with rifles and not cooperating with the NYPD detectives,” he said.
“ICE needs to get the f— out of here,” Public Advocate Jumaane Williams, who was also at the scene, seethed. “Nobody wants it.”
“Everybody said that this would happen,” he said of the shooting.
NYPD cops ultimately had to escort the ICE agents away from the scene as a growing mob cursed at the federal agents from the other side of the police tape.
ICE agents have often been criticized for their heavy-handed tactics when they arrest undocumented immigrants. Arrests by ICE in New York State rose by nearly 70% over the summer from 927 in May to 1,567 in July, according to federal data compiled by the Deportation Data Project. There have also been several high-profile incidents where agents shot, wounded, or killed protesters, such as in Minneapolis in January when ICE agents fatally shot Renee Good.
The New York Immigration Coalition said that more than two dozen people have been shot by federal immigration officers in the last year across the country.
“ICE’s violent tactics are a clear danger to all New Yorkers, as today’s shooting in a residential neighborhood demonstrates,” Murad Awawdeh, the president of New York Immigration Coalition, said in a statement. “This incident is another reminder of the unchecked, rampant violence ICE has been spreading throughout our communities.”
“We demand an immediate investigation into the shooting, the release of the body camera footage, and accountability for any ICE agents who used excessive force,” Awawdeh said. “We must abolish ICE and strengthen the safety of all New Yorkers.”

sources.news_title: ICE agents nearly hit child as they open fire on man in NYC clash
sources.text:
Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents shot and wounded a man in a car on a bustling New York City street Thursday afternoon, narrowly missing a child who was seated in the vehicle and sparking a heated confrontation between the feds and outraged citizens, officials said.
ICE agents opened fire on the silver Honda Civic at about 4 p.m. on Marble Hill Ave. near W. 225th St. in the Bronx. The shooting victim was in the SUV when he was hit, according to sources.
Public Advocate Jumaane Williams, who showed up at the scene, was told by NYPD detectives that “there was a toddler in the car.”
“I’m just trying to locate the child,” he said. “What about this is about public safety?”
A video reviewed by the Daily News shows NYPD officers carrying the wounded man from the silver SUV and putting him into the back of a black car, which sped off.
A man with a federal badge around his neck sporting an assault rifle was in the middle of the street, asking witnesses taking video of the scene to back away, the video showed.
The man who was shot was taken to an area hospital and is “conscious and receiving medical attention,” the NYPD said on X.
The NYPD “was not involved in the incident,” the tweet said.
Outraged Bronx residents flocked to the corner, chanting “Murderers!” “F— ICE!” and “ICE out of the Bronx!”
During one heated exchange, more than a dozen people grabbed and pinned a masked ICE agent against a wall when he got too close to the police tape lining the scene.
“Take the mask off P—-!” the residents screamed.
NYPD officers swooped in and rescued the agent, pulling him back behind the tape as federal agents created a blockade line.
The NYPD referred all additional questions about the incident to the feds.
But Assemblyman Manny De Los Santos, D-Manhattan, who showed up at the scene, was told that ICE agents weren’t cooperating with the NYPD.
“The ICE agents are over there with rifles and not cooperating with the NYPD detectives,” he said.
“ICE needs to get the f— out of here,” Williams seethed. “Nobody wants it.”
“Everybody said that this would happen,” he said of the shooting.
A Department of Homeland Security spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The New York Immigration Coalition said that more than two dozen people have been shot by federal immigration officers in the last year across the country.
“ICE’s violent tactics are a clear danger to all New Yorkers, as today’s shooting in a residential neighborhood demonstrates,” Murad Awawdeh, the president of New York Immigration Coalition, said in a statement. “This incident is another reminder of the unchecked, rampant violence ICE has been spreading throughout our communities.”
“We demand an immediate investigation into the shooting, the release of the body camera footage, and accountability for any ICE agents who used excessive force,” Awawdeh said. “We must abolish ICE and strengthen the safety of all New Yorkers.”

Man injured after New York shooting involving DHS agents
sources.text:
Man injured after ICE shooting in New York
October 9, 2026
A man was shot by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent during an arrest in New York City, US federal authorities and Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Thursday.
The shooting occurred at around 4 p.m. local time (2100 GMT) in the Marble Hill neighborhood of Manhattan.
The New York Police Department said its officers were not involved in the incident and that the man was conscious and receiving medical attention at a nearby hospital.
US President Donald Trump's administration has scaled up ICE raids in major US cities to detain and deport people who are in the US illegally.
Mamdani urges Trump to end ICE actions in NYC
New York City Mayor Mamdani condemned the shooting and said he had contacted President Trump.
Mamdani added that a five-year-old child was reportedly in the car during the shooting, but that the child was "physically unharmed."
"This is an unconscionable and incredibly serious situation," Mamdani said in a post on X. "I have called the President; when we speak I will demand that he ends all ICE enforcement actions in our city. I will not stand by while ICE agents terrorize our communities."
New York Governor Kathy Hochul said she had spoken with Trump and Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin about the shooting. DHS is the parent agency of ICE.
"I expressed outrage on behalf of New Yorkers and urged them to halt ICE enforcement operations in New York," Hochul said. "I also asked that any body camera footage of the shooting be released to the public so we can establish the facts and get to the truth."
Federal govt says 'criminal illegal alien' in hospital receiving treatment
In a post on X, DHS had confirmed that an "ICE officer discharged his weapon" during an attempt to arrest a "criminal illegal alien from the Dominican Republic" with ties "to the Trinitarios gang."
DHS said the man had a prior conviction for grand larceny and had been arrested "multiple" times for assault, robbery, possession of drugs, and weapons possession.
DHS noted ICE officers immediately rendered aid after the man was injured. "The individual is alive and at a local hospital," the statement said, adding that the FBI was on the scene.
ICE, CBP fatal shootings raise alarm in second Trump term
Deadly ICE and Border Patrol shootings have drawn major controversy during Trump's second term, particularly regarding the training and oversight of the agents.
An ICE agent killed a 37-year-old US citizen, Renee Good, during their operations in Minneapolis in January, triggering demonstrations there and in several other US cities.
Later that month, Alex Pretti, another US citizen, was killed by two US Customs and Border Protection officers agents in Minneapolis following an altercation.

sources.news_title: Federal agents shot and wounded a person in New York Tuesday, police say
sources.text:
Federal immigration officers opened fire on a Dominican man in New York because he drove his car into officers' vehicles and they believed their lives were in danger, a senior Immigration and Customs Enforcement official said Friday.
The 28-year-old man, whom New York City police identified as Oscar Belgal, was shot "superficially" in the neck as ICE officers attempted to arrest him, Marcos Charles said.
Officers used their vehicles to block the man as he attempted to drive away, but he accelerated toward them, Charles said during a news conference with U.S. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin in Washington. The Department of Homeland Security said the news conference was about the "dangerous consequences of sanctuary city policies."
"Our officers, using their training and believing that their life and the life of the partners and the general public were in danger, used their training and fired weapons," Charles said.
Belgal had a 5-year-old boy in the car with him when the shooting happened, officials said.
Mullin said ICE agents didn't know the child was in the car, but that Belgal "was aware" and chose to knowingly put the boy at risk by trying to evade officers.
ICE had issued a detainer on Belgal, who runs with a gang known for thefts using weapons and mopeds, Charles said.
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and New York Gov. Kathy Hochul, both Democrats, said late Thursday that they had pressed Mullin and Republican President Donald Trump to release Belgal, to no avail. They also urged the administration to immediately release body camera footage of the shooting and to halt immigration enforcement operations in the city.
Mullin said Belgal is being held in a facility outside New York City but declined to provide the location. He confirmed ICE officers were wearing body cameras that were activated, but didn't say when any footage would be released.
Protesters and local officials had decried the shooting as an example of the dangers of the Trump administration's immigration crackdown.
RELATED NEWS | Chicago woman who was shot 5 times by immigration agent files lawsuit alleging he fired from behind
"There is no justification for what we have seen today," Mamdani said late Thursday at the scene of the shooting.
Federal officers who surrounded the vehicle wore construction vests and masks, making it difficult to identify them as immigration officers, he said.
New York City Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said Belgal was pulling into a parking space when a federal officer in plainclothes approached with gun drawn, followed by another federal officer who also wasn't in uniform. Belgal started to pull the car forward, and at least one of the officers fired seven rounds, hitting the man below his left ear.
Much of Mullin's remarks Friday were reserved for excoriating Mamdani and his immigration policy.
"Sanctuary politicians, they create an environment for criminal activity to thrive, not for the American citizens to be safe," he said.
Mullin said ICE has asked local officials in New York to hold onto more than 14,000 people for federal officers to collect and place in immigration detention.

"Silence. Absolute silence is what we have gotten back," he said. "Why would they release these individuals back onto the streets?"
"We're enforcing our nation's laws. We're not picking and choosing," Mullin continued. "Why is that controversial? We should all want law and order on our streets."
Mullin also criticized the attention surrounding the case.
"This was a thug. The absolute worst of the worst," he complained. "We're giving so much attention to this thug."

sources.news_title: ICE agents shoot man in front of his five-year-old son in New York
sources.text:
US3 min(s) read
ICE agents shoot man in front of his five-year-old son in New York
Officials have confirmed that a US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent shot a man as he drove in a car with a child in New York City.
The man has been identified as Oscar Belgal, 28, and he was driving with a five-year-old boy, believed to be his son, in the vehicle.
Belgal survived the shooting and has been treated at a hospital.
As reported by Sky News, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) didn't describe what led to the shooting.
They stated that 'during the incident, an ICE officer discharged his weapon', with the man injured in the aftermath.
DHS further stated that they were looking to arrest the man as part of a 'targeted enforcement operation', but protesters and local authorities said it was another example of the threats posed by the Trump administration's immigration crackdown.
How the incident unfolded
According to Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch, Belgal pulled into a parking space when a federal officer in plain clothes approached him with their gun drawn.
Another federal officer did the same, also out of uniform.
The man moved forward when at least one of the officers fired seven rounds, striking Belgal below his left ear.
Tisch further detailed at the press conference on Thursday (October 8) that the child was unharmed and with a relative, before highlighting that police weren't involved in the operation.
However, they responded after hearing shots.
A statement from the DHS claimed that they were looking to arrest a 'criminal illegal alien' who had a grand larceny conviction and a history of other arrests.
Mayor Zohran Mamdani speaks out against ICE
Speaking during the aftermath, Mamdani powerfully claimed: "There is no justification for what we have seen today."
"Early reports indicate agents surrounded (the man) and a five-year-old child in his car before firing multiple rounds," he added.
The Mayor of New York explained that the federal officers who surrounded the vehicle wore construction vests and masks, which made it harder to identify them as ICE officers.
He further added that he'd spent two hours pushing Donald Trump and Homeland Security secretary Markwayne Mullin to release Belgal.
Mamdani further urged ICE to halt operations in the city, adding that their agents removed the man from the hospital and took him away on Thursday.
Outrage from the public
Tisch revealed that while an NYPD security camera recorded some of the lead-up, it did not capture the shooting.
Gunfire sounded around 4 pm local time in Marble Hill, an area of Manhattan attached to the Bronx.
Democrat city council member Carmen De La Rosa, who represents areas including Marble Hill said they 'are heartbroken and enraged' at the situation at a heated news conference at the scene of the shooting.
Protesters could be heard chanting, 'ICE off our streets now', before marching to the hospital where Belgal was being treated, as clashes at the barricades ensued.
There were multiple arrests, while a damaged car blocking the roadway was seen with small holes in two windows, as Tisch explained that a bullet's entry point was on its front windshield, and its exit point was in a rear window.
Since 2025, ICE agents have fired their guns at over 12 vehicle stops, with at least four people paying with their lives, and several others left injured.
